ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Report and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 19725, as amended, effective 28 September 2024) and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions (Act No. 10464, as amended); Commercial Act (Act No. 8404, as amended), Articles 289, 292 and 317; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 9467, as amended), Article 16; Financial Transactions Reports Act; Regulation on Financial Companies' Detection of Suspicious Transactions; Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) Notice on Beneficial Ownership Information and Financial Services Commission supervisory guidance.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Corporate Registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registry Office (Beopwonsa) of the Republic of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: obtain a certified copy from the Supreme Court Registry, notarize before a civil notary, then request an apostille from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) of the Republic of Korea. Consular Legalization (non-Apostille countries only): notarize, then submit to the Korean embassy or consulate in the jurisdiction of issuance for legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are alternative, mutually exclusive paths and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Status of Corporate Registration/Settlement of Taxes)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: District Court Registry or the Korean National Tax Service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: request the certificate from the relevant District Court Registry or National Tax Service, notarize the issued copy, and obtain an apostille from MOFA. Consular Legalization: for a certificate issued in a non-member state, notarize the document and then obtain legalization from the Korean mission competent for the issuer's location. The two methods are parallel and exclusive; combining them is not permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing incorporation and bank account opening
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate board of directors of the parent entity or the beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille: notarize the board resolution or power of attorney at a notary public in the issuer's jurisdiction and obtain an apostille from that jurisdiction's competent authority (e.g., Secretary of State or MOFA). Consular Legalization: if the issuer is located in a non-member state, notarize the document and legalize it through the Korean embassy or consulate. Only one path may be used per document; do not chain apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum of Association / Articles of Incorporation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean law firm drafting the articles, authenticated by a civil notary and registered with the Court Registry Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For use outside Korea: notarize the sealed articles and obtain an apostille from MOFA. For use inside Korea: provide a certified Korean translation of the registered articles; no apostille is needed for domestic use. If the Articles were issued outside Korea, the document must be apostilled if the issuer state is a Hague member, or consular-legalized if the issuer state is not a member. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution where the beneficial owner, parent entity, or existing corporate group holds an account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be notarized by the issuing bank's legal officer or a notary public. If the bank's jurisdiction is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, the letter must be apostilled by that state's competent authority; if the jurisdiction is a non-member state, the letter must be consular-legalized by the Korean embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives; sequential chaining is prohibited.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before engagement, every applicant, ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), director, and person authorized to sign must undergo continuous screening against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC's Specially Designated Nationals List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the United Kingdom's HM Treasury Sanctions List, and the domestic sanctions and counter-proliferation lists administered by the Korean Ministry of Economy and Finance and KoFIU. The compliance officer must verify customer identity using a valid government-issued document, identify any PEPs or close associates, apply enhanced due diligence, document the reason for any risk rating, and report any suspected match to KoFIU as an STR within 48 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Government e-court registry (Iros, www.iros.go.kr) - Trade Name Search and Registration System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory trade name of a chusik hoesa must be written in Hangul. A foreign-owned company may adopt a transliterated Hangul name and may also record an English trade name in the registry. The name must correspond to the actual line of business, be sufficiently distinctive within the same municipality, and end with the legal-form suffix 주식회사 (Chusik Hoesa). Identical or confusingly similar names are rejected. The four-tier naming structure is: geographical descriptor + distinctive element + business purpose + legal form.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registry rejects a name, the applicant must receive a written statement citing the specific conflicting provision. Within seven days after notice, the applicant may file an immediate administrative appeal with the head of the local district court registry, using the prescribed form and attaching the rebuttal, evidence of prior registration, or an explanation of changed circumstances. A judge will render a ruling, and a further appeal to the Supreme Court is possible within fourteen days. Legal counsel is advisable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mailbox facilities are generally rejected for a government affairs advisory. Under the Commercial Act, a chusik hoesa must have a physical address that appears in the registry; the National Tax Service requires an actual workplace for VAT and corporate tax filings, and Korean banks will refuse to open a corporate account if the registered address is a virtual office or P.O. box. A shared office or coworking space with a dedicated office number, a genuine lease contract, and actual employee presence may be acceptable, but a virtual-only address is not permitted for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for on-site inspection: visible company nameplate, physical office desk and equipment, active employee occupancy, lease agreement in the company's name, and original business formation documents available on site. Risk: Medium-High. The municipal tax office and the district court registry may conduct unannounced inspections, particularly for companies with an ISIC code involving government relations and lobbying, to verify genuine operational substance. During the first year after incorporation, the probability of a physical site visit is estimated at 30-40%.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Court registration tax on incorporation (assumed paid-in capital of USD 100,000; rate 0.4% under Local Tax Act)
Legal fee for preparation of Articles of Association, name clearance, and incorporation filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a standard chusik hoesa incorporation (USD 1,500-3,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization bundle (five instruments)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Civil Notary Public and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (apostille) or Korean embassy/consulate (consular legalization)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notary Fee Act schedule plus MOFA apostille fee of USD 20 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Korean translation of corporate documents (five instruments)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark at USD 150 per document for 10-15 pages

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Administrative filing agency fee for document delivery and registry submissions
Trade name search and availability check via iros
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee; free public access

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 288, 289, 290, 295, 317, 318, 329, 330, 332, and 361 with respect to incorporation, capital stock, share issuance, registered office, and statutory officers of a Chusik Hoesa; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (Act No. 5559, as amended), Articles 2, 4, 5, 6 and 9 for foreign-invested stock corporation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea, Court Registration Office (Deung-gi-guk) operating the electronic registration portal 'IRO (Internet Registration Office)' at www.iros.go.kr, with administrative oversight by the Ministry of Justice Business Registration Division and the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) Invest Korea One-Stop Service for foreign investors.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) and Certificate of Incorporation Registration Application (Hoesa Seollip Deunggi Sinsacheong), submitted together with the minutes of the promoters' general meeting and the certificate of subscription of shares; a separate Application for Approval of Foreign Investment (Oegugin Tuja Singo/seong) may be required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: The Commercial Act sets no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, the paid-in capital must be at least KRW 1 (approximately USD 0.00075) and full payment or contribution of the par value of subscribed shares must be made through a designated bank account before incorporation; capital may remain in the corporate operating account upon registration, but if structured as a foreign-invested entity under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a certificate of foreign-currency inward remittance (entry of foreign capital) must be deposited with a foreign exchange bank and reported, without requiring a statutory escrow lock-up beyond preservation of capital funds until incorporation registration is completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION IN WRITING OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [●] CHUSIK HOESA (the 'Company'), INCORPORATED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. The undersigned, being the sole first director or all of the first directors of the Company, convened and adopted the following resolutions by unanimous written consent in lieu of an actual board meeting on this [●] day of [●], 20[●], at the Company's registered office. WHEREAS the Company was duly incorporated as a stock corporation under the laws of the Republic of Korea, and its registration of incorporation was completed upon the admission of the Court Registration Office on [●] 20[●]; WHEREAS the Company requires immediate corporate governance actions to enable the lawful conduct of its business, including the subscription and payment of share capital, the establishment of banking relations, the maintenance of a registered office, and the appointment of statutory officers; WHEREAS the Board is authorized under the Company's Articles of Incorporation and Article 343, Article 393 and related provisions of the Commercial Act to issue shares and to delegate operational matters to officers. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that: 1. SHARE CAPITAL. The Board hereby confirms that all authorized shares issued on incorporation have been fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation, and the initial paid-up capital is [●] Korean won, none of which has been retired. The Board directs management to ensure that shareholder registry entries and share certificates are executed under the corporate seal. 2. BANK ACCOUNTS. The Company shall open, maintain, and operate corporate bank accounts with such banks as the Representative Director may select. The President and Representative Director is hereby authorized, jointly with the Company's accounting officer, to execute all account-opening documents and to authorize wire transfers. All account signatories must comply with the Bank for International Settlements/Korean anti-money laundering rules and the Real Name Financial Transaction Act. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office of the Company shall remain at [●], Republic of Korea, which shall be the seat of the Company for all statutory, tax, and judicial notices. The corporate seal shall be registered with the Court Registration Office and, where required, with the tax administration. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board appoints [●] as Representative Director, [●] as Statutory Auditor or Audit Committee members, and [●] as secretary. The Representative Director shall have day-to-day management powers, excluding any matters reserved to the Board under applicable law. 5. GOVERNMENT RELATIONS BUSINESS. The Company is authorized to engage in business consulting and cross-border trade policy advisory services, including government relations liaison activities that comply with the Public Official Election Act, the Foreign Bribery Prevention Act, and the Improper Solicitation and Graft Act. 6. DELEGATION. The Representative Director is authorized to execute all instruments, negotiate contracts, hire employees, and procure such professional advisors as are necessary to implement these resolutions. APPROVED AND ADOPTED by the first directors on the date first written above. [Signature blocks, corporate seal, and anti-money laundering acknowledgment to follow.]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain foreign investment report and inward remittance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (Invest KOREA) or the domiciled foreign exchange bank designated under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding shareholder, if a non-resident, must file a Foreign Investment Report (Oegugin Tuja Singo) prior to or simultaneously with the inward remittance of capital, using the Foreign Investment Promotion Act protocol. The investor must open a temporary account in the name of the planned corporation at a domestic foreign exchange bank, remit the capital amount from overseas in the investor's own foreign-currency account, and instruct the bank to issue a Certificate of Foreign Currency Deposit (Oegugin Hwansong Ipgeum Jeungmyeongseo). The certificate must state the subscriber, the remitting bank, the date of remittance, and the exact Korean won amount converted at the certified exchange rate. The Report must also include the investor's declaration of non-involvement in prohibited Korean industries and the intended business scope under ISIC 7020. The bank will submit the report electronically to the Ministry of Economy and Finance via the Korea Financial Telecommunications & Clearings Institute. If the investment is less than KRW 100,000,000, no prior approval is required, but the certificate is still mandatory. The formation counsel must not proceed to step 2 until the certificate and the Report receipt number, or a ministry confirmation slip, are in hand. If the report is challenged for incomplete payee or source-of-funds documentation, the counsel must submit a written supplemental statement with the bank's anti-money laundering officer and obtain a corrected certificate before expiration.
required_dossiers: Passport or national identity card of the foreign shareholder (certified true copy)
Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association of the foreign corporate shareholder, translated and apostilled or consular-legalized
Foreign Investment Report Form (attached to the Foreign Investment Promotion Act) signed by the investor
Inward remittance instruction and source-of-funds statement
Power of attorney authorizing the local formation counsel
Certificate of foreign-currency deposit issued by the Korean foreign exchange bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the foreign investment report is returned or suspended, the counsel must file a written supplement within 14 calendar days, providing the missing bank statements, proof of beneficial owner identity, and a corrected power of attorney. If the deposit certificate contains a currency or date error, the bank must reissue the certificate after re-verification and such cure shall not count against the applicant. In the event of a ministerial objection based on the sensitive nature of government relations consulting, the investor must narrow the business description and resubmit the report under the same foreign-investment file number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and notarize the Articles of Incorporation and convene the promoters' general meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public (Buin), and the Court Registration Office as the ultimate filing recipient through the IRO portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Formation counsel must prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation (Jung-gwan) including the corporate name, the precise business purpose limited to ISIC 7020 (cross-border trade policy analysis and foreign stakeholder lobbying advisory), the address of the registered office, total authorized shares, class of shares, par value, incorporation date, and the number of directors and auditors. The Articles must be notarized by every promoter or by a duly authorized proxy, with the notary verifying identity and the legality of the clauses. Immediately after notarization, the promoters shall convene a general meeting of the promoters for the election of the first directors and statutory auditor and for the establishment of the capital contribution ledger. The first director(s) shall then adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution as set out in the legal framework. All meeting minutes, the notarized Articles, the subscription application, and the consent-to-accept-office declarations must be assembled in a single electronic dossier and certified by the formation counsel as consistent under the Commercial Act. A minimum of one director must maintain Korean residency. The counsel should upload the pre-registration package to the IRO portal for preliminary verification of the corporate name and registered office availability.
required_dossiers: Notarized Korean-language Articles of Incorporation
Minutes of the promoters' general meeting electing directors/auditor
Written acceptance of office signed by each first director and auditor
Share subscription applications and payment record for each promoter
Certificate of foreign-currency deposit or proof of domestic paid-in capital
Corporate seal certificate or seal imprint certificate for the planned entity
Passport copies and resident registration certificates of the first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRO portal issues a provisional rejection because of an illegal business purpose clause, the notary must amend the Articles and obtain fresh promoter signatures. If a director's residency condition fails, the shareholder meeting must replace the director before registration. If the notary demands a translation of the foreign investor's identification, counsel shall submit a notarized Korean translation within five business days. Any suspension of the uploaded dossier due to missing minutes can be cured by re-filing a signed corrigendum and paying the nominal correction fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation registration application with the Court Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of the Republic of Korea, Court Registration Office through the IRO electronic registration system under the Registration of Real Estate Act and Commercial Registration Rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The formation counsel shall submit the application for incorporation registration (Hoesa Seollip Deunggi Sinsa), attaching the notarized Articles, the minutes of the promoters' general meeting, the report of shares subscribed and paid, the certificate of payment deposited at the bank, the written appointment consents of directors and auditor, and the engraved corporate seal imprint certificate. The application must be electronically signed with the counsel's accredited digital certificate and stamped with the corporate seal or the promoter's seal. The registration fee, computed at global rates of 0.4 percent of paid-in capital, must be paid by South Korean e-payment through IRO, with the official domestic court fee not exceeding KRW 225,000; the estimated USD 180 assumes the minimum capital structure. The tax office registration as a business operator will later be automatic under the Commercial Registration data linkage. Upon acceptance, the Court will issue the Certificate of Incorporation Registration (Deung-giwon), which will include the registration number, the corporate name, the registered office, the directors, and the seal. Counsel must verify that the registered business purpose in the certificate is limited to advisory and consulting activities not constituting regulated brokerage or legal services. The full statutory incorporation is deemed complete only when the competent court registry has entered the corporation into the Commercial Registry.
required_dossiers: Application for incorporation registration on the prescribed court form
Notarized Articles of Incorporation (original or certified copy issued by the notary)
Minutes of the promoters' general meeting and the first board meeting resolution
Share subscription certificates and capital contribution ledger
Certificate from the bank confirming payment of the capital amount
Written acceptance of office of each director and statutory auditor
Corporate seal imprint certificate (Inin-jeungmyeong)
Power of attorney and identification of the formation counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration application is returned for supplementary submission (bojeong myeongnyeong), the counsel must complete the missing document within the statutory cure period of one to four weeks as stated in the IRO notice. If the court questions the adequacy of the capital payment evidence, counsel must obtain a bank confirmation letter or ledger extract showing the funds remain in the corporate account. If the court rejects the business purpose as too broad, counsel must amend the Articles and file a corrected registration without requesting a refund. Should the court issue a suspension, an objection and correction application under the Civil Procedure Rules can be filed within two weeks.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the corporate income tax enterprise status and obtain corporate bank, VAT, and withholding tax registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) business tax office having jurisdiction over the registered office, and the chosen commercial bank under the Real Name Financial Transaction Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 60 days of incorporation, the Representative Director must file the business registration certificate application with the NTS, using the Court registration data to receive a business registration number (Saeupja Deungrok). The Company must then obtain an electronic tax certificate, issue a corporate seal certificate at the bank, and open the permanent corporate operating account with the initial capital funds, transfer the provisional account balance into the permanent account, and obtain a check card. For government relations advisory contracts where the Company expects annual taxable revenue, the NTS will register the Company for VAT, corporate income tax, and employee wage withholding. The Company must also file a report under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act if it maintains the foreign investor registration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. Counsel should ensure the corporate bank onboarding information includes ultimate beneficial owners, the source-of-funds declaration, and an anti-money laundering risk categorization consistent with the Medium-Risk_Enhanced tier. The bank shall perform a sanctions screening against OFAC, EU, UN, and South Korean lists; the formation counsel must confirm no adverse hit before completion.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation Registration (Deung-giwon)
Corporate seal imprint certificate and corporate seal card
Business registration application (Saeupja Deungrok Sinsaseo)
Identification and resident or alien registration certificates of all officers
Foreign investment report confirmation from the Ministry of Economy and Finance
Certificate of bank account and capital payment
Utility bill or lease contract proving the physical registered office at the posted address
AML/KYC questionnaire of the Company, shareholders, and directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS flags the company for having no physical substance or for a suspicious government relations purpose, counsel must submit a lease contract, fixed cost schedule, and client engagement letters to the tax office and request reconsideration. If the bank rejects the corporate account due to enhanced due diligence, counsel shall supply a definitive ownership chart and audited bank statements of the foreign parent, or designate a Korean-resident director as an authorized signatory. If the foreign investment report confirmation is delayed, counsel must present the bank receipt and a later-dated confirmation to complete KYC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) and the municipal city/county licensing division where the registered office is located, with the Government Public Official Election Commission and the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission (ACRC) as regulatory overseers for permissible lobbying and foreign-agent disclosure matters
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Consulting and Business Support Service Business Registration (as a business registration under the Commercial Act) and Foreign-Invested Business Registration; a statutory trade or industrial license is not required for the rendering of advisory and policy analysis, but the corporate entity must hold an NTS Business Registration Certificate, register with the National Election Commission as an incidental political opinion poll or interest-group reporting entity only if applicable, and meet the license conditions of the Public Official Election Act and the Improper Solicitation and Graft Act for government stakeholder engagement. A Foreign Agent Registration Act-style filing is not currently mandatory in Korea except for specific foreign government projects; the firm may nevertheless be required to register as a lobbyist under the Act on the Regulation of Lobbying Activities resolving, but if physical campaign distribution or polling is conducted, a political survey permit from the National Election Commission is mandatory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MoE) of the Republic of Korea, Environmental Impact Assessment Division, through the Environmental Administrative Agency of the provincial government where any physical branch is located; if no physical manufacturing or construction activity takes place, the EIA is limited to the office-based desktop review permit 'Environmental Registration for Small-Scale Business' (Exclusion)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt: ISIC 7020 government affairs and lobbying advisory is a service-sector category with no construction, manufacturing, effluent, or point-source emission footprint. The company is only required to obtain the NTS business registration and, if a lease covers more than 300 square meters or if employee canteens generate food waste, apply for a simplified waste disposal contract with the local municipal EIA-related administrative office. A full Environmental Impact Assessment under Article 22 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act is Not Applicable. The company shall not host campaign events exceeding 1,000 participants that would trigger a temporary crowd-safety and noise-control notification under the Local Government Public Health and Noise Control Ordinance.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial wastewater discharge (no process effluent); volatile organic compounds limited to trace office cleaner evaporative losses and must remain below 5 mg/m3 at the property boundary if a fume-generating office equipment cleaning operation is installed; no hazardous waste generation threshold applies, but any printer toner cartridges and batteries must be recycled under the Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) rules with a waste-recycling manifest above 200 liters per month. Office noise shall not exceed 65 dBA during daytime at the lot line. For any ancillary café or pantry generating food waste above 100 kg per month, the company must enter a licensed food-waste collection contract with the municipal authority and keep disposal manifests for two years.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification (Green Card) issued by the municipal fire department and the Korea Fire Industry Technical Institute for the leased Class II office premises, including a biennial fire safety inspection of exits, extinguishers, and sprinklers, a structural load safety certificate for the office fixtures if the tenant fit-out exceeds 1,500 kg/m2 floor loading, and an Occupational Safety and Health General Workplace Registration under the Occupational Safety and Health Act if the company employs five or more workers, including emergency exit drills, a safety manager appointment, and a workplace risk assessment every six months; if the registered office is a suburban business center with no kitchen and fewer than five employees, only the fire-safety inspection certificate and the building management's civil defense pass are required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal is the HomeTax system (www.hometax.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that commences business in Korea, establishes a permanent establishment, or otherwise derives Korean-sourced income must register for a Business Registration Number (BRN), which simultaneously serves as the VAT registration number, Corporate Income Tax number, and withholding tax account number. The foreign corporation must appoint a resident tax representative or domestic agent where required by the National Tax Basic Act. The application is filed with the competent District Tax Office through the NTS HomeTax portal or in-person by an authorized agent. Required evidence includes the foreign entity's articles of incorporation, a certificate of foreign registration or equivalent existence document, a board resolution appointing the Korean agent and authorizing registration, a power of attorney in favor of the domestic representative, documentary evidence of the Korean place of business, and the statutory Korean business registration application completed in the Korean language. The NTS reviews the submission and issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number within a statutory processing period. Registration must be completed within 20 days from the date of business commencement, opening of a Korean blue-chip commercial presence, or the date on which the non-resident becomes liable for VAT or Corporate Tax in Korea.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not maintain a check-the-box regime. A Chusik Hoesa incorporated in Korea is automatically treated as a domestic corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax on its worldwide income. Foreign entities are classified as domestic or foreign corporations strictly under the Korean Corporate Tax Act based on statutory headquarters and place of effective management. No hybrid mismatch election is available; anti-hybrid rules prescribed under the Korean Tax Act and OECD-aligned implementation will apply to deny unintended deductible outcomes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean VAT Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold applies to corporations. Every taxable person, including a Chusik Hoesa, is mandatorily required to register for VAT through the Business Registration Number before or within 20 days after commencing taxable business activity, irrespective of projected revenue. Simplified taxpayer classification is available only to certain individually owned service businesses with annual taxable turnover below KRW 48 million, and this does not apply to a joint-stock corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-invoice) regime under the NTS HomeTax system. All VAT invoices issued by a Chusik Hoesa must be prepared in electronic form through the official HomeTax e-invoice service, a licensed accounting program, or an NTS-integrated API channel, unless a narrow statutory paper invoice exemption applies. Every e-invoice is transmitted to NTS in real time and must receive an automatic internet transmission confirmation number before it is treated as legally issued. The NTS captures invoice data through API, applies digital signature and electronic stamping requirements, and reconciles the transmitted data against the VAT return pre-filing system. Failure to transmit an e-invoice through the system is treated as failure to issue a valid tax invoice and attracts the statutory additional tax under the VAT Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating is available under the Korean VAT Act for exported goods and qualifying cross-border services. For goods, the exporter must complete a Korean Customs Service export declaration using the UNI-PASS system, the goods must physically depart Korea and be delivered to a foreign buyer, the export declaration must be in the name of the taxable entity, and the consideration must be paid in foreign currency by a non-resident. For services, including government affairs lobbying and cross-border trade policy advisory services supplied by a Chusik Hoesa to a foreign principal, zero rating applies only where the service recipient is a foreign non-resident and the service is actually used or consumed outside Korea. Domestic lobbying performed on behalf of a foreign client to influence Korean government action, or services used by a permanent establishment in Korea, remain taxable at 10% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration issued via Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from Korea
Commercial invoice and underlying export sales contract signed by the foreign buyer
Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation (Inward Remittance Certificate) from a licensed Korean foreign exchange bank
Proof of payment received in foreign currency corresponding to the export invoice
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly verify export zero-rating claims by matching UNI-PASS export declarations, the e-invoice transmission database, and foreign exchange purchase/settlement records reported by Korean banks through the Foreign Exchange Information System. Any zero-rated supply lacking a valid export declaration, missing foreign exchange receipt within the 180-day repatriation deadline (unless a lawful extension is obtained), or otherwise failing to satisfy statutory zero-rating conditions will be reclassified as taxable, and the VAT is immediately clawed back with interest. Fraudulent zero-rating claims, false customs declarations, and fictitious export documentation additionally incur an evader additional tax commonly equal to 40% of the underlying VAT amount, late payment surcharges, and criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act. For serious export fraud, the responsible directors and tax agents may be jointly and severally liable, and the statutory collection period is extended to a maximum of ten years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK); foreign exchange supervisory authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act is primarily the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), with monitoring and enforcement delegated to the Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) and designated foreign exchange banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a dualist foreign exchange control regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Current account transactions are substantially liberalized: trade settlements, service fees, dividends, and salaries can be remitted freely after a licensed foreign exchange bank performs an underlying transaction review to verify the business reality and the accuracy of the designated foreign exchange purpose code. Capital account transactions, including equity subscriptions, loans, and securities investments, are subject to a report-and-monitor system rather than a prior licensing regime for most direct foreign investment, but directional restrictions and post-transaction reporting obligations may apply under the Capital Transactions Regulations. The Korean won is convertible for current purposes but is not freely tradable offshore; cross-border KRW settlement is restricted to residents and designated settlement accounts, compelling non-residents to fund their capital injections in USD, EUR, JPY, or CNY. Dividend remittances to non-resident shareholders are approvable once audited financial statements, tax withholding certificates, and proof of a properly registered foreign investment are presented; a bank will reject the remittance if the company has not completed its statutory external audit, has unresolved tax arrears, or cannot demonstrate a legitimate capital base. There is no central-bank rationing system, but the FSS enforces strict underlying transaction and suspicious-transaction checks, and the Bank of Korea operates the large-value payment and settlement infrastructure. On balance, the Korean regime is administratively monitored and transparent rather than stringently controlled; no mandatory currency surrender or conversion quota applies to current receipts, but counterparty banks have full discretion to demand documentary proof.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree, export proceeds must be repatriated and settled within six months from the export declaration or shipment date, unless a bank-approved extension is granted for deferred-payment or long-cycle exports. Proceeds must be received through a designated foreign exchange bank and credited to either a Korean won account or a foreign currency deposit account. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: the exporter may retain foreign currency freely in a domestic foreign currency deposit account, but the receipt must be reported and confirmed through the Foreign Exchange Information System and by the bank, and the Korea Customs Service may require a proof of receipt when verifying trade settlement eligibility. Any failure to meet the six-month collection timeline without a valid extension creates a legal block to future export financing and VAT export incentives.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Low to not viable as a primary treasury rail. Under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, a non-bank electronic money institution is not authorized to open a Korean won deposit account with the full legal attributes of a corporate demand deposit account or to execute the statutory foreign investment registration and capital verification procedures required for a Chusik Hoesa. Offshore fintech EMIs such as global business account providers are not licensed by the Financial Services Commission as foreign exchange banks, so they cannot submit the mandatory Foreign Exchange Information System reports, issue foreign investment deposit certificates, or perform the underlying transaction verification required for Korean corporate banking. An EMI may be used only as an ancillary payment channel for small service-related outflows if the actual funds are ultimately settled through a domestically licensed designated bank; however, inbound capital injection, dividend remittance, and regulatory capital verification must be handled with a Tier-1 domestic commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the initial corporate account opening of a Korean Chusik Hoesa, the appointed statutory director and the primary authorised signatory must generally appear physically at a designated domestic branch in Korea. Remote consular proxy opening is not a standard legal route for a newly formed stock corporation; most Tier-1 banks require face-to-face passport verification, proof of address, and a branch interview with the beneficial owners. Foreign directors may be accommodated only after the initial account is open, and additional signatories may be added through notarised powers of attorney or video-call KYC procedures. The bank will also ask for the corporate seal certificate, the certificate of incorporation, the articles of incorporation, and a resolution of the board appointing the bank signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed person (PEP) and foreign influence risk arising from the government affairs and lobbying related classification of ISIC 7020.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide current passports of all statutory directors and material beneficial owners; a PEP questionnaire signed by each UBO; a certified group ownership chart; the Korean business license and any statutory licence for government relations advisory work; a compliance manual showing that activities are limited to cross-border trade policy analysis and foreign stakeholder communications, with an explicit prohibition on domestic public official lobbying; a detailed expense and gift policy compliant with the Kim Young-Ran Act; and executed retainer agreements with the ultimate client names to prove the counterparty is not a sanctioned government or entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear economic substance of foreign investors injecting equity into the Chusik Hoesa, especially if the parent company is located in a shell-financing jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the parent company's audited financial statements for the past three years; six months of original bank statements from the remitting account; a source-of-wealth letter signed by the ultimate shareholder; tax clearance certificates from the parent company's jurisdiction; board resolutions authorising the equity subscription; the share subscription agreement; a bank reference letter; and a sworn declaration that the funds do not originate from third-party, bearer-share, or anonymous pass-through accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Risk of trade mispricing or false advisory revenue where the company reports high-value lobbying/consulting fees without tangible deliverables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide executed service agreements with non-resident clients; itemised invoices and payment certificates; detailed timesheets, research reports, or policy memoranda demonstrating actual deliverables; the Korean electronic tax invoice issued for each retainer; the VAT return filed with the National Tax Service; external audit confirmation of the revenue recognition policy; and an arms-length transfer-pricing assessment showing that the retainer fees match market rates for trade policy advisory services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to prove that the statutory corporate purpose is compatible with Korean financial-sector licensing and AML obligations for government relations work.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the certified articles of incorporation expressly limiting the corporate purpose to ISIC 7020 trade policy consultancy and foreign stakeholder engagement; the Korean business licence; a declaration from the tax representative confirming no concurrent unlicensed financial activity; an internal AML/KYC policy; each international client's corporate registry extract and beneficial ownership statement; and a letter from the duly appointed compliance officer stating that no direct political contribution will be made using corporate funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital for the Chusik Hoesa must follow the Foreign Investment Promotion Act route. The non-resident investor should first file a foreign investment notification with a designated domestic bank or KOTRA and obtain a foreign investment registration signal, then transfer the equity subscription amount from an offshore shareholder account via SWIFT MT103 into the Foreign Currency Investment Deposit Account opened at the chosen Tier-1 domestic bank. The payment message must carry the appropriate Foreign Exchange Information System purpose code for direct equity investment and the corporate beneficiary name exactly matching the Korean business registration. Upon receipt, the bank issues a certificate of foreign investment, which is then used to obtain the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate and to satisfy the capital verification requirement through the certified external auditor. For an already-incorporated company, the capital increase must also comply with the Korean Commercial Act by amending the articles, filing the registry, and issuing shares only after the subscription price is fully paid into the bank. Funds must not be split into multiple unnamed deposits, as the full remittance trail must support source-of-funds review and the later dividend remittance approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound retainer payments for cross-border trade policy and lobbying services should be cleared using SWIFT MT103 from the company's Korean won or foreign currency settlement account, with a purpose code matching current account service transactions and underlying advisory agreements retained for five years. For merchandise trade, the entity may use commercial letters of credit issued by the domestic bank in favour of foreign sellers, with the bill of lading and shipping documents negotiated under a complying presentation, or documentary collections on D/P and D/A terms where the bank acts as collecting agent. All outbound disbursements, whether fees or trade proceeds, are subject to the bank's underlying transaction review, and the company must present invoices, contracts, customs declarations where applicable, and beneficiary due-diligence information before the bank executes the transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward exchange contracts with a designated foreign exchange bank for hedging identified KRW/USD, KRW/EUR, KRW/JPY, or KRW/CNY trade and investment exposure up to 12 months, provided the underlying receivables or payables are documented and the transaction is reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with licensed Korean banks or through an approved international NDF market only when the corporate has genuine forecast foreign exchange exposure and the position is demonstratively non-speculative; pure carry or directional trades are prohibited for domestic Korean corporates.

Cross-currency swaps and interest rate swaps concluded with a domestic bank as hedge for foreign-currency denominated debt, equity valuation exposure, or long-term service contracts, subject to prior bank approval, board authorisation, and capital transaction reporting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return with audited or tax-basis financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via Hometax electronic filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal year ending December 31, on or before March 31 of the following year; for a fiscal year ending on any other date, within 3 months of the fiscal-year close, except that if the close falls in the first 10 days of a month, the filing deadline is compressed to 2 months after that closing date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers an additional tax of 10% of the deficient amount, plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest on unpaid corporate income tax; prolonged non-filing can result in NTS assessment, asset seizure, revocation of business registration, and, for a persistently inactive company, court-ordered dissolution under the Korean Commercial Act on grounds of continued non-operation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) for approval of balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement, and allocation of retained earnings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Recorded in the company minute book and board minutes at the registered office; no government authority receives a separate fee-bearing filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within 3 months after the end of each fiscal year, i.e., by March 31 for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa; financial statements must be laid before the AGM at least 1 week in advance if the company keeps a statutory auditor.

stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM by the statutory deadline permits the court, upon petition by shareholders or the Minister of Justice, to order convocation; responsible directors may be subject to administrative fines under the Commercial Act, and the absence of shareholder approval makes the annual financial statements incapable of supporting a clean statutory audit opinion.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax top marginal rate plus 10% local corporate income tax surtax, producing an all-in top effective rate of 26.4%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Under the Tax Incentive Limitation Act and Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a qualifying high-tech foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa located in a Free Economic Zone may obtain a 100% exemption from national and local corporate income tax for 5 years and a 50% reduction for the next 2 years; R&D tax credits for new-growth engine industries can reach 20-25% of qualifying R&D expenditure; job creation and facility investment tax credits are also available.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Base and Tax Return (법인세 과세표준 및 세액 신고서) filed via the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal; attached financial statements, tax adjustment schedules, international transaction schedules and transfer pricing documentation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year, no later than March 31 of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: registered trade name, business registration number, head office address, representative director, statutory tax representative, and fiscal year-end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Chusik Hoesa incorporated in South Korea is a resident corporation even when all shareholders are non-residents. The company must maintain a valid Korean business registration; a non-resident director who has no Korean residential address must designate a tax representative in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Capital and ownership composition: paid-in capital, number of issued shares, shareholder name, nationality, ownership percentage, and resident or non-resident status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Fully disclose all non-resident shareholders and identify whether they are beneficial owners. The absence of minimum capital does not eliminate the obligation to declare actual paid-in capital; retained earnings and shareholder distribution history must be traceable for dividend withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business classification and statutory license: Korean Standard Industrial Classification code corresponding to ISIC 7020, business scope, license number, and description of cross-border trade policy analysis and government relations advisory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For ISIC 7020 government affairs and lobbying activities, the company must identify the statutory authorization for lobbying and must not classify unlawful lobbying payments as deductible service expenses. Non-resident ownership does not excuse compliance with Korean licensing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net income before tax as reported under K-IFRS for the Chusik Hoesa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All gross retainer-wire and bank-transfer income from both domestic and foreign clients must be included. The entity is tax-resident in Korea and therefore subject to worldwide income taxation; no exclusion is permitted for cross-border lobbying fees retained offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income reconciliation: add-backs of nondeductible expenses, deduction of nontaxable income, and application of statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees, royalties, and advisory service charges paid to foreign affiliates must satisfy the Korean arm's length standard. Bribes, penalties, illegal lobbying contributions, and fines imposed on a director are nondeductible and must be added back.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base computation after applying allowable loss carryforward and exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Utilize only losses that meet the statutory carryforward period and continuity-of-business requirements. For an ordinary corporation the carryforward limit is 10 years, and 15 years for qualifying small and medium-sized enterprises; foreign merger or ownership changes may restrict loss usage.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National corporate income tax computed under the progressive schedule applied to the final taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 9% bracket, 19% bracket, 21% bracket, and 24% top bracket as applicable. If the entity has an approved Free Economic Zone tax holiday, attach the exemption schedule and properly allocate exempt versus non-exempt income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit and withholding tax credits on foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach official foreign tax payment certificates and calculate the credit limitation as the Korean corporate income tax attributable to foreign-source income. Non-resident shareholders are not entitled to use this credit against their own dividend withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local corporate income tax surtax computed at 10% of the national corporate income tax, plus any special tax surcharges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The local corporate income tax is a separate liability of the Korean legal entity. A non-resident shareholder cannot assume or pay the local tax on behalf of the corporation without triggering additional underpayment penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedules of international transactions and transfer pricing: cross-border related-party contracts, service fees, royalties, interest, notional adjustments, and transfer pricing documentation checklist.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the aggregate cross-border related-party transaction amount reaches KRW 10 billion during the fiscal year, the Local File and Master File must be prepared and filed with the tax return or upon request. For a government-affairs advisory company, the core income-generating functions are the staff who perform policy research, regulatory engagement, negotiation, and implementation in Korea; those functions cannot be relocated to a shell affiliate without Korean tax consequences.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident remittance and withholding schedule: dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, and other outbound payments paid to non-resident persons.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The payer is legally required to withhold at statutory rates before remitting dividends, interest, or royalties to a non-resident beneficial owner. To apply a tax treaty rate, the payer must obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership documentation before the remittance date.

stage_6.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing of the annual corporate income tax return attracts an additional tax equal to 20% of the unpaid tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes; underreported tax returns attract 10% additional tax, and fraudulent underreporting attracts 40%; late-payment surcharges accrue daily until full payment. Failure to submit transfer pricing documentation can trigger separate administrative penalties under the Law for Coordination of International Tax Affairs, and criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act is punishable by imprisonment of up to 5 years or a fine of up to 3 times the tax evaded.
